text.p: Italian debt markets stood their ground against a fairly grim European backdrop, with some relief coming in the shape of a proposed Italian mini-budget but plenty of nervousness over EMU and its prospects.

Despite EMU worries crowding in to chip away at Italian bonds, the March Btp future on LIFFE managed to remain three basis points on positive ground at 129.70 while the benchmark November 2006 Btp was 15 basis points up at 104.08.
The spread over the benchmark Bund was 176 basis points, not as bad as the worst moments on Tuesday when it splayed beyond 180. The most traded July 2006 Btp fell four bps to 109.21.
The lira battled valiantly back from perilously close to the 1,000 per mark watershed to be quoted at 995.35/5.75.
But the debt outlook was not great. "The Btp market is bearish short term with support at 129.20 and resistance at 130.15," a senior broker at an Italian bank in London said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he would launch a mini budget of structural measures in coming weeks to tackle Italy's budget deficit and slap it down to size to meet EMU criteria on time. The market liked the idea but now awaits details, and a vital ally, Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti, warned he would not support tax hikes or spending cuts.

Analysts said there was little of a significantly structural nature Prodi could use which would take effect quick enough to shrink the deficit to three percent of GDP by the year end, as stipulated in EMU criteria, and they cited political hurdles Prodi will have to leap to force a package through.

But they also pointed out Italian markets' worst worry was likely to be not whether Italy would make EMU criteria on time, but whether Germany would do so and if it did, whether the prospect of having Italy squeezing in too might not make it decide to delay the whole project.
